title: Birds and Charlie 'Yardbird' Parker
summary: Johnston asks about birds in Gil's music, tells a painting story and Gil explains Parker's nickname.

story.theme_name: Charlie Parker, Dizzy and the bebop revolution
story.community_name: Charlie Parker: encounters, lore and legacy

blocks.x: Do you have a special affection for birds?

I just seem to feel this, in your work. My husband was a painter and he painted a very rhythmic, geometrical thing as a matter of fact called 'Tribute to Yardbird'. And he was talking about Yard Bird Parker. And I always lecture to my own students in let erature about art, we both taught in the same college.

This particular occasion there was an art exhibition and he had some paintings in it and Yard Bird was there. And I thought I had talked about abstraction and rhythm and everything else in painting. So I took my students there and I was looking at something else with some of them and one student came running over and she said, oh Mrs. Johnston, I've found it, I've found it! I said, you've found what? She said, I've found the bird. (LAUGHTER).

So I'm not saying that about your music, but as I've said it's an impressionistic kind of thing. (LAUGHTER). I really thought that I would give up teaching.
